body:
@hpvb @deralmas We should update https://github.com/hpvb/dynload-wrapper/ to add these IWYU pragmas automatically to the wrapped includes.

clangd / IWYU would report the `so_wrap.h` files as "not used directly" because what's used from them in most cases is structs or enums from the thirdparty headers. Using the `export` pragma, IWYU now considers that the `so_wrap.h` file is providing those symbols directly.

After #116693 these are no longer necessary, our wrapped `windows.h` takes care of setting it.

Due to some reordering of includes caused by this PR, I started getting errors about redefining `WIN32_LEAN_AND_MEAN` due to it already being defined by one of our `egl.h` includes.

Misc issue reported when I had forgotten to turn off all diagnostics but unused headers. This is flagged on templates builds as this virtual method is `#ifdef`ed in `object.h`. There might be more such occurrences, I just fixed the couple that were in my report for Android templates IIRC.

body:
If this needs to only be added to the header and not the implementation, this patch will do:

```diff
diff --git a/generate-wrapper.py b/generate-wrapper.py
index 62b6294..77abc12 100755
--- a/generate-wrapper.py
+++ b/generate-wrapper.py
@@ -146,9 +146,9 @@ def generate_header(sysincludes, functions, initname, implementation_headers):
 
     for include in sysincludes:
         if include.startswith("<"):
-            retval.append(f"#include {include}")
+            retval.append(f"#include {include} // IWYU pragma: export.")
         else:
-            retval.append(f"#include \"{include}\"")
+            retval.append(f"#include \"{include}\" // IWYU pragma: export.")
 
     for function in functions:
         retval.append(f"#undef {function}")
```

Will make a PR upstream.

Apparently even with the `export` pragma in that file, it wasn't enough to silence warnings from clangd.
But with angled brackets it treats it like a black box / system header so it's fine. This probably makes sense to use for all thirdparty headers and our wrappers for them.
While poking at Windows drivers, I took the opportunity to try to use smaller headers than `windows.h`. A bit of scope creep...
